 Thursday, October 22, 2026 
CDC COCA Call Today: What Clinicians Need to Know about Dengue in the United States
 #19,382
 Later today (Thursday, Oct 22nd) the CDC will hold a COCA Call for clinicians and other healthcare professionals on this year's record breaking spread of Dengue in Florida (see chart above).
 Carried and spread by mosquitoes, Dengue fever first returned to Florida in 2009 after an absence of nearly 70 years  (see 2010 MMWR report Locally Acquired Dengue --- Key West, Florida, 2009--2010).   
 The virus was likely imported by someone with recent travel to a dengue endemic region who served as a blood meal for a local mosquito, which then began spreading the virus to others.  
 Initially, more than 2 dozen Dengue patients were identified in and around Key West in the fall of 2009, although a year later, the CDC would report far more people were exposed (see CDC Press Release Report Suggests Nearly 5 Percent Exposed to Dengue Virus in Key West). 
 This year, the Florida Department of Health has recorded nearly 300 imported cases ( see chart below), with the vast majority linked to Cuba.  
 This year's locally acquired outbreak is the largest reported by Florida since the 1940s. While this may seem primarily a ` Florida problem' -   this is a tourist state - and doctors anywhere in the country (and internationally ) could see Dengue cases arising from this outbreak.   Accordingly, the CDC will hold a COCA (C linician Outreach & Communication Activity ) call this afternoon. While these presentations are often technical and are of greatest interest to clinicians and healthcare providers, they are usually archived within a few days, and made available to the general public. Details on today's presentation follow: 
 What Clinicians Need to Know about Dengue in the United States 
For Health Care Providers
 Oct. 22, 2026, visit link for details. 
 At a glance 
During this COCA Call, presenters will discuss current dengue epidemiology in the United States and review dengue clinical features, current diagnostic testing recommendations, and clinical management guidelines.
 Overview
Dengue virus is endemic in several U.S. territories and freely associated states and has caused increasing numbers of travel-associated and locally acquired dengue cases in U.S. states in recent years. No preventative medicines or specific antiviral treatments are available for dengue. Severe dengue is a medical emergency—recognition of warning signs and appropriate clinical management are critical for reducing severe outcomes. During this COCA Call, presenters will discuss current dengue epidemiology in the United States and review dengue clinical features, current diagnostic testing recommendations, and clinical management guidelines.
 Webinar 
 Call Details 
 Date & Time: Thursday, October 22, 2026 - 2:00 – 3:00 PM ET

 Call Objectives 
COCA Call Objectives 
At the conclusion of the session, the participant will be able to accomplish the following: Cite background information on the topic covered during the presentation. 
 Identify CDC's role in the topic covered during the presentation. 
 Describe the topic's implications for clinicians. 
 Identify concerns and issues related to preparedness for and response to urgent public health threats. 
 Identify how an interprofessional team of healthcare providers can work with patients to promote disease prevention. 
 Activity-specific Objectives 
At the conclusion of this session, the participant will be able to accomplish the following: Summarize dengue epidemiology and transmission in the United States. 
 List the clinical features of dengue. 
 Explain dengue diagnostic testing for patients with suspected dengue. 
 Describe appropriate treatment for dengue patients according to severity classification.
